## Body

F190/#279 lessons (reviewers broke round 1 with executable probes; all of these were real):
- Record a durable INTENT event before the first write, carrying the SCOPE (project, role, instance). A redo finishes only recorded intents (no backfill of history) and takes scope from the intent, never from what the index shows after a partial write.
- Key completion by the intent seq (the done event names it), not by the seat id: ids come back (revive) and cross new boundaries.
- Never split one logical index change across two SQLite transactions (end old rows, then insert new ones): a cancelled task between them strands work. One store method, one txn. Rebuild index rows from the governance files on rerun, so "git has it, index has neither" heals.
- Supersede chains: two /clears queued before the first async carry means the named successor is already dead. Follow the boundary chain to the live end (same spawn_id every hop), and prove every hop again inside the store txn.
- Requeueing work (delivered->queued) needs claim to skip answered requests, or a late answer gets redelivered.
- Probes: hold EventBus::publish_committed_batch with a Notify to freeze a task at the publication boundary, then abort it = a realistic cut. A mutation that "survives" often means the test drives a path (New) where the guard doesn't matter; retarget the test at the path that reads it (Redo).
- Shared target etiquette: leave ~30 s between your builds when reviewers queue (shared-build polls at 20 s and misses short releases).
